01 / Installation

On your Mac.

The current Mac test build is for Apple Silicon (M-series Macs), with macOS 13 or later.

  1. Open the CommonCopy .dmg file.
  2. In the installer window, drag CommonCopy.app onto the Applications folder shortcut. Copy the application, not the DMG file.
  3. Open CommonCopy from Applications. The manager opens and a clipboard icon appears in the menu bar at the top of your screen.
  4. In CommonCopy Settings, enable Command + right-click. When requested, enable CommonCopy in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, then return to CommonCopy.
  5. In Finder, eject CommonCopy Installer using the eject symbol beside it under Locations. Run the installed application from Applications.

To update: choose Quit CommonCopy from its menu-bar icon, copy the new application into Applications, and choose Replace. Your phrase library is stored separately and should be kept.

On your Windows PC.

The current Windows test package is for Windows 10 or 11 on x64 PCs.

  1. For a portable ZIP, choose Extract All. Keep the entire extracted folder together in a permanent location, then open CommonCopy.exe. Do not run it from inside the ZIP.
  2. If supplied with a setup installer instead, run it and follow its installation steps. Start CommonCopy from the Start menu afterward.
  3. Find the clipboard icon in the notification area beside the clock. You may need to open the hidden-icons arrow.
  4. Click into an editable text field, hold Ctrl and right-click to open your phrase menu. The default keyboard alternative is Ctrl + Shift + Space.

To update a portable copy, quit CommonCopy from its tray icon before replacing the application files. Keep your saved phrase data. Unsigned private builds may show a Windows security warning; verify the source before opening them.

02 / Everyday use

Save it once. Paste it forever.

Save highlighted text

  1. Highlight selectable text in another application.
  2. Use Command + right-click on Mac or Ctrl + right-click on Windows, then choose Save highlighted text…. The keyboard alternative on Mac is Command + Shift + Space.
  3. Review the text and title, choose a category, and click Save.

After a successful phrase Save, the editor and manager close automatically. CommonCopy keeps running. Cancel does not save a phrase; a save error leaves the editor open.

Paste a saved phrase

  1. Click exactly where you want the text in your email, document, chat, or editor.
  2. Open the compact menu using your platform’s activation gesture.
  3. Open a category and choose a phrase. CommonCopy returns to the source application and sends the paste shortcut.

Use Manage phrases to search, add, edit, or copy text manually. An ordinary right-click keeps its usual behavior.

Make room for your prompts

Use Prompts as a parent category, then add GPT, Image based, or a project name beneath it.

Mac: open a category’s options and choose Add subcategory. Windows: choose Add category from the category options, then set Parent category to Prompts.

Select the subcategory, choose Add phrase, and enter a short title and the full text. Prompts are saved text; CommonCopy does not send them to an AI service.

Find it again

Favourites brings together phrases you have starred. Commonly Used ranks phrases by use count, then recent use. Search in the manager checks titles and phrase text.

A disabled phrase stays in your library but is unavailable for insertion. Enable it from its phrase options when you want to use it again.

03 / Practical examples

Useful words, ready to go.

Save any of these as a phrase, then paste it into the appropriate application. Replace bracketed instructions yourself; CommonCopy pastes literal text and does not fill variables or run code.

Prompts / GPT

A clearer email

Rewrite the email below in a warm, concise tone. Preserve the facts, dates, and commitments. Return only the revised email.

[Paste email here]

Prompts / Image based

A product photograph

Create a clean studio photograph of [product] on an off-white background, with soft side lighting and a subtle contact shadow. Keep the product proportions accurate. No lettering or watermarks.

Prompts / Website project

A focused code review

Review the code below for correctness, accessibility, and error handling. Prioritize concrete issues, explain their impact, and suggest the smallest useful fix.

[Paste code here]

Day-to-Day

A practical follow-up

Hi [name],

Just checking in on [topic]. Could you let me know the current status and the next expected step?

Thanks,
[your name]

Code

A JavaScript helper

const unique = (items) => [...new Set(items)];

Paste this into your editor for review. Saving or pasting code does not execute it.

04 / Troubleshooting

Get back to your words.

Mac: Command + right-click does not open CommonCopy
  1. Confirm CommonCopy is running: look for its clipboard icon in the menu bar.
  2. Open its Settings and make sure Command + right-click is enabled.
  3. Enable CommonCopy under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, then return to the utility. Hold Command while you perform the secondary click (including a two-finger trackpad click).
  4. If this started after replacing a private build, quit CommonCopy. Remove its old Accessibility entry with the minus button; add CommonCopy from Applications again with the plus button, enable it, and reopen it. Toggling a stale entry alone may not help.

Command + Shift + Space is an alternative for opening the menu. Accessibility permission is still required for selection capture and automatic paste.

Windows: the gesture or keyboard shortcut does not work

Confirm the tray icon is present and Settings → Enable Ctrl + Right Click is selected. Check the configured keyboard shortcut; another application may already use it. Try the gesture in a regular Notepad window. CommonCopy may be unable to paste into an application running as administrator; test a normal window rather than elevating the utility.

The menu opens, but a phrase does not paste

Click an editable field before opening CommonCopy, then choose the phrase again. On Mac, check Accessibility permission. Protected fields and some applications restrict automated paste. Use Copy in Manage phrases, return to the destination, and paste manually. On Windows, Settings includes a paste delay; a slower application may need a longer delay.

Save highlighted text is empty or unavailable

Select text that the source application can actually copy. A picture, scanned PDF, password field, or protected page may not offer selectable text. Re-select it in the original app and use the activation gesture or shortcut; avoid changing focus before capture. On Mac, check Accessibility permission. You can also copy text yourself and add it through Add phrase.

The manager disappeared after I clicked Save

That is expected after a successful phrase Save. Your phrase is saved and CommonCopy remains running. Reopen Manage phrases from the menu-bar or tray icon, or use the activation gesture when you need the compact menu.

How do I quit or reopen CommonCopy?

Closing the manager does not quit the utility. On Mac, use the clipboard icon in the top menu bar. On Windows, use the clipboard icon beside the clock (check hidden icons). Choose Manage phrases to reopen the manager or Quit CommonCopy to exit. A Terminal command is not required.

Mac: a private test build will not open

Current private builds are ad-hoc signed and are not yet notarized. First use the app-specific Open Anyway option in System Settings → Privacy & Security, if offered.

For the trusted private build supplied directly by the CommonCopy maintainer, the known repair below applies only to that installed application. Quit the old copy first. Do not use it for an unknown download.

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/CommonCopy.app"
open "/Applications/CommonCopy.app"

This removes quarantine from this app only. Never disable Gatekeeper system-wide. A damaged-app or malware warning needs investigation; do not assume every launch warning is this private-build issue. Developer ID signing and notarization remain required work before public release.

My phrases seem missing after an update

Confirm you are running the intended copy of CommonCopy and using the same computer account. Quit duplicate copies. Do not delete the data folder, reset your library, or overwrite it with an empty import. Keep a copy of the existing data before investigating. If you have an exported library, review it before importing.

05 / Your library

Local. Yours. Worth backing up.

On Mac, use Settings → Export. On Windows, use Library → Export library…. Keep the exported JSON somewhere safe before updating or moving computers. Importing is a library replacement operation; export the current library first and read the confirmation.

Your saved phrases are separate from the application:

  • Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/CommonCopy/phrases.json
  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\CommonCopy\phrases.json

The automatic previous-version backup rotates; it is not a lasting archive. CommonCopy does not synchronize between computers automatically. Your library is readable local JSON, not encrypted secret storage. Keep passwords, recovery codes, and access tokens in a password manager.

The help included with the utility opens locally in your browser and works offline.

04 / QuestionsA few things to know.

Common questions.
Clear answers.

What can I save?

Reusable text: replies, sign-offs, AI prompts, code snippets, links, and more. Add a title and organize it under categories and subcategories.

Does it need an account or internet connection?

No. The desktop utility works locally, without an account or network connection. You can export and import your phrase library yourself.

Does it replace normal right-click?

No. Use Ctrl + right-click on Windows or Command + right-click on Mac to open CommonCopy. An ordinary right-click keeps its usual behavior. A keyboard shortcut is also available.

What permissions does the Mac version need?

Accessibility permission enables Command + right-click, selection capture, and pasting into another application. You choose whether to grant that access. Some protected or unusual text fields may restrict copy or paste.

Can I keep passwords in CommonCopy?

CommonCopy stores phrases as readable local text. Use a dedicated password manager for passwords, authentication codes, access tokens, and recovery keys.

Will there be advertising?

Only on this website. The desktop app stays ad-free. No ad provider is connected to this preview; provider information and any required choices will be added before advertising starts.

Can I download it now?

Public downloads are not open yet. Both platforms are being tested privately while the installation experience and final checks are completed.

Website advertising

A little support. No interruptions in the app.
